q: The word 'punch' most likely comes from the Hindi 'panch', meaning what?
r: Five, for the drink's five parts: spirit, sugar, lemon, water and spice. It sailed to Europe with East India Company crews.

q: The Gin & Tonic began life as what?
r: Officers drank bitter quinine tonic against malaria; the gin ration made it bearable.

q: Which of these is NOT a genuine Old Fashioned variation?
o: Oaxaca Old Fashioned made with prosecco
Oaxaca Old Fashioned made with mezcal and tequila
Benton's Old Fashioned with bacon-fat-washed bourbon
r: The Oaxaca Old Fashioned uses reposado tequila and mezcal, never prosecco. The other three are all real, documented drinks.

q: A Patiala peg is named after a Maharaja of Patiala. What is it?
o: A whisky served with soda in a silver cup
A peg measured against a polo mallet
A double shot chased with lassi
r: An oversized measure, attributed to Maharaja Bhupinder Singh, whose hospitality left visiting cricket teams unfit for the morning.

q: India Pale Ale got its name from what?
o: The long sea voyage to India it had to survive
r: Brewers hopped and strengthened the ale so it would survive the months-long sail to India. It was never brewed there.

q: Why does the EU refuse to call most Indian 'whisky' whisky?
o: It is usually distilled from molasses, not grain
It is aged for under a year
r: Most IMFL whisky is molasses-based, so the EU classes it differently. A billion people call it whisky at the table anyway.

q: The Negroni was reportedly created when Count Camillo Negroni asked for what?
o: His Americano made with gin instead of soda
r: He asked for the Americano stiffened with gin in place of soda water, in Florence around 1919.

q: What makes a Negroni 'Sbagliato'?
o: It is served long over ice
r: Sbagliato means 'mistaken': a Milanese bartender reached for sparkling wine instead of gin and kept it.

q: Urrak, available only for a few months a year, is which stage of feni?
o: A blend of cashew and coconut feni
r: Urrak is the light first distillation, available roughly March to May, and almost never leaves Goa.

q: How did the cashew, source of Goan feni, reach India?
o: The Portuguese brought it from Brazil
The British brought it from Africa
It is native to the Western Ghats
Dutch traders brought it from Indonesia
r: The Portuguese carried it from Brazil to Goa in the 1500s, which makes feni a four-hundred-year-old fusion drink.

q: In a Martini, what does ordering it 'perfect' mean?
o: Equal parts dry and sweet vermouth
r: Perfect splits the vermouth half dry, half sweet. Dry means less vermouth; dirty adds olive brine.

q: Which is the correct build for a classic Sazerac?
o: Rye or cognac, sugar, Peychaud's bitters, absinthe rinse
Rye, sugar, Angostura bitters, vermouth rinse
r: New Orleans' Sazerac: spirit, sugar, Peychaud's, and an absinthe rinse. Peychaud's is the signature, not Angostura.

q: Judima, which won a GI tag in 2021, is made by which community?
r: The Dimasa people of Assam. It was the first traditional brew of the Northeast to get a GI tag.

q: Why are Mumbai's older bars called 'permit rooms'?
o: A 1949 law technically required drinkers to hold a permit
They needed a special licence to serve after midnight
Only permit-holding clubs could serve foreigners
They were permitted to serve only IMFL
r: The Bombay Prohibition Act of 1949 required a drinker's permit. The law faded; the name never left.

q: Which statement about dilution in cocktails is correct?
o: A properly shaken drink is 20–25% water from melted ice
Dilution should be avoided entirely in quality cocktails
Stirring adds more water than shaking
Dilution only matters for drinks served over ice
r: Melted ice is an ingredient. That water softens the alcohol and knits flavours; shaking dilutes more than stirring.

q: The Moscow Mule's copper mug originated as what?
o: A 1941 marketing pact between three struggling sellers
A Prohibition-era way to hide the drink
r: A vodka importer, a ginger beer maker and a copper mug seller pooled unsold stock in 1941.

q: Arrack, once southern India's everyday spirit, takes its name from an Arabic word meaning what?
r: From araq, meaning sweat, for the condensation dripping off the still.

q: Which is true of the Aviation cocktail?
o: Its blue-violet tint comes from crème de violette
Its colour comes from blue curaçao
r: Gin, maraschino, lemon and crème de violette, which gives the pale sky tint. It's shaken and strained.

q: Sharab, the Hindustani word for liquor, shares an Arabic root with which two English words?
r: All from shariba, to drink. One verb, three very different evenings.

q: What distinguishes a Collins from a Fizz?
o: A Collins is served tall over ice; a Fizz is shaken, often with egg white, and served shorter
A Fizz uses gin; a Collins uses whiskey
A Fizz is stirred, not shaken
r: Both are sours lengthened with soda, but the Collins is tall over ice while the Fizz is shaken hard, often with egg white, and served without much ice.

q: Kerala's toddy shops, the kallu shaapus, are also famous for what?
r: The kappa, karimeen and duck curries exist to keep pace with the toddy.

q: Which is the correct order of the Sour template?
o: 2 parts spirit, 1 part citrus, 1 part sweet
1 part spirit, 2 parts citrus, 1 part sweet
3 parts spirit, 1 part citrus, 2 parts sweet
1 part spirit, 1 part citrus, 2 parts sweet
r: 2:1:1 is the skeleton of the Daiquiri, Whiskey Sour, Margarita and Gimlet.

q: The Espresso Martini was created in 1980s London by which bartender?
r: Dick Bradsell, reportedly for a model who asked for something to wake her up, then mess her up.

q: Amrut's name comes from amrit, which in Hindu legend is what?
r: The nectar of immortality, churned from the ocean. A drinkable pun with scripture behind it.

q: Which claim about the Bloody Mary is accurate?
o: It was first mixed in 1920s Paris and renamed Red Snapper at New York's St. Regis
It was invented at New York's St. Regis and renamed in Paris
It was created in London during the Blitz
It was named for Queen Mary I by her own bartender
r: Harry's New York Bar in Paris in the 1920s; the St. Regis later adopted it and politely renamed it.

q: Sekmai yu, a distilled rice liquor, is named after what?
o: The clay pot it ferments in
The festival it is drunk at
r: Sekmai, a village in Manipur so associated with the drink that its name became the drink's.

q: What is the correct role of a 'rinse' in cocktail making?
o: Coating the glass with a strong ingredient, then pouring off the excess
Diluting a spirit with water before serving
r: A few millilitres of absinthe or smoky whisky coats the glass for aroma without weight.

q: Which is India's oldest surviving beer brand, brewed at Solan since the 1850s?
r: Lion, brewed in the Himalayan foothills at Solan, is considered Asia's oldest surviving beer brand.

q: In cocktail terms, what does 'expressing' a citrus twist mean?
o: Snapping the peel to mist its oils over the drink
Squeezing the juice into the drink
Twisting the peel into a spiral garnish
Rubbing the peel around the rim only
r: Snap the peel skin-side down over the surface to mist aromatic oils. It's seasoning, not decoration.

q: Kanji, the deep-purple Holi-week drink, is fermented from what?
r: Black carrots and mustard seeds left to ferment in the winter sun: North India's homemade kombucha.

q: What is the difference between shochu and soju?
o: Shochu is Japanese, soju is Korean
Shochu is brewed, soju is distilled
Shochu is rice-only, soju is never rice
r: Both are distilled East Asian spirits: shochu from Japan, soju from Korea.

q: The Indian Army's rum ration is traditionally which style?
r: Dark XXX rum has warmed high-altitude postings for decades, and Old Monk built its legend in those canteens.

q: Which is true of the Paper Plane, a modern classic from 2008?
o: It is equal parts bourbon, Aperol, amaro and lemon
It is equal parts gin, Aperol, amaro and lime
It is stirred and served up with no garnish
r: Equal parts bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino and lemon juice. Named after the M.I.A. song.

q: Why was the sherry cobbler historically important?
o: It was the first drink served over crushed ice
It was the first cocktail sold in bottles
r: The most fashionable drink of the 1800s, and it single-handedly popularised the straw.

q: Neera and toddy are the same palm sap at different stages. What separates them?
o: Fermentation: neera is fresh and sweet, toddy has fermented
Distillation: toddy is distilled, neera is not
The time of year they are tapped
r: Morning sap drinks sweet as neera; by evening it has fermented into toddy on its own.

q: Which spirit is the base of a Pisco Sour?
o: Pisco, a South American grape brandy
r: Pisco is a grape brandy from Peru and Chile, shaken with lime, sugar and egg white.

q: Handia, brewed by Adivasi communities of eastern India, is what?
o: A rice beer fermented with herbal starter tablets
r: Rice beer fermented with herbal ranu tablets, offered to guests and gods alike.

q: What is a 'dry shake' for?
o: Whipping egg white or aquafaba into foam before shaking with ice
Shaking without spirits to test balance
r: Shake once without ice to build foam, then again with ice to chill. That's how sours get their dense white crown.

q: Which best describes the Highball ratio?
o: 1 part spirit to 2–3 parts cold mixer, built over plenty of ice
1 part spirit to 1 part mixer, shaken
2 parts spirit to 1 part mixer, stirred
1 part spirit to 5 parts mixer, no ice
r: Precision matters more than it looks: flat, warm or over-poured highballs fail.

q: In the Northeast, zutho and apong are both what?
o: Rice brews, Naga and Mising respectively
Millet spirits, Naga and Mising respectively
r: Rice becomes zutho for the Nagas and apong for the Mising of Assam, each with hereditary starter cakes.

q: Which is true of vermouth once opened?
o: It should be refrigerated and used within about a month
It keeps indefinitely like a spirit
It must be frozen to stop oxidation
r: It's wine. Refrigerate it and use it up; a dusty room-temperature bottle ruins Martinis.

q: Rajasthan's royal houses were known for distilling what?
o: Heritage liqueurs of saffron, dates and dry fruits
r: Recipes like kesar kasturi, with saffron, dates, dry fruits and dozens of spices, survived the palaces and are bottled again today.

q: Why is 'Old Fashioned' a retronym?
o: 1880s drinkers asked for their whiskey cocktail made 'the old-fashioned way'
It was renamed after Prohibition ended
It was the oldest drink in the first cocktail book
It referred to old-fashioned glassware, not the drink
r: Tired of newfangled liqueurs and garnishes, drinkers asked for it made the old-fashioned way, and the name stuck.

q: Irish Coffee was invented where?
r: Invented at Foynes in the 1940s to thaw transatlantic passengers, then perfected at the Buena Vista in San Francisco.

q: Coorg is known for a distinctive household drinking tradition. What is it?
o: Homemade wines from coffee, ginger and gooseberry
r: Homemade wine is a household art there, and weddings are judged partly on the house pour.

q: What does 'GI tag' mean for a drink like feni or Judima?
o: Geographical Indication: only producers from that place may use the name
Grain Identified: a labelling rule for the base ingredient
r: Geographical Indication, the same protection Champagne enjoys.

q: The palm civet's nickname 'toddy cat' comes from what?
o: It raids the sap pots tied under palm blossoms
Its call sounds like a tapper's whistle
It was kept as a pet in toddy shops
r: It raids the collection pots toddy tappers tie under palm blossoms, and has a taste for the fermented ones.

q: Which is the correct distinction between bitters and amari?
o: Bitters are dosed by the dash; amari are sipped or poured in measures
Amari are non-alcoholic; bitters are not
Bitters are always Italian; amari are not
r: Bitters are intense tinctures used as seasoning; amari are bitter liqueurs consumed in real measures.

q: Goa's port-style fortified wines are a legacy of what?
o: Four and a half centuries of Portuguese rule
r: No Goan susegad lunch is complete without a small glass of it.

q: What is the difference between a strain and a double strain?
o: A double strain adds a fine mesh to catch pulp and ice shards
A double strain means straining twice into two glasses
A double strain uses two Hawthorne strainers
A double strain is straining before and after chilling
r: Add a fine mesh strainer over the glass when pulp, herb flecks or ice shards would spoil a stemmed drink.

q: Terracotta stills found in the Gandhara region suggest distillation in South Asia dates back how far?
r: Roughly two thousand years, among the earliest evidence of distillation anywhere.

q: The Singapore Sling was created at which hotel?
r: The Long Bar at Raffles, around 1915, where sweeping peanut shells onto the floor is still encouraged.

q: India's craft gin wave of the late 2010s rose mainly out of which state?
r: Goa, distilled with local botanicals like gondhoraj lime, Himalayan juniper and curry leaf.

q: What does 'susegad', often linked to Goan drinking culture, mean?
r: From the Portuguese sossegado: a relaxed, unhurried contentment. It's a way of drinking as much as a mood.

q: Gondhoraj lebu, prized in modern Indian cocktails, is associated with which region?
r: Kolkata's beloved gondhoraj lime turned the gimlet into a modern Indian bar classic.
